2.content:
This SOW covers METRO’s SAP CLOUD ALM Technical Monitoring Change Request Management implementation from January 2026 through October 2026, aligned to the S/4 RISE migration plan, including tenant onboarding, standard change management, technical monitoring setup, production deployment, and hypercare transition to the METRO team.

- Establish SAP Cloud ALM for Technical Monitoring and Change Request Management across the agreed landscape and monitoring use cases.
- Configure and validate change workflows, transport governance, non-production monitoring, alerting, dashboards, and production integration in line with the delivery timeline.
- Enable operational handover to METRO through training, documentation, and transition support during deploy and hypercare.

Deferred decisions, dependencies, and project-specific conditions are set out in Section 10 (Key Assumptions) and Section 21 (Key Observations).

3.1.content:
METRO is establishing SAP Cloud ALM for Technical Monitoring and Change Request Management as part of its S/4 RISE migration plan. The current landscape requires a standardized SaaS-based ALM approach that supports hybrid operations, transport governance, monitoring, dashboards, and alerting across the relevant SAP systems and integrations. Key pain points addressed by this engagement include fragmented monitoring, limited end-to-end visibility across systems and interfaces, and the need to move from legacy ChaRM and operational practices toward standardized Cloud ALM processes before Solution Manager 7.2 reaches mainstream end.

The business drivers for this engagement are to reduce migration effort, enable governed change cycles from development through production, improve operational visibility for system health, jobs, user performance, and integrations, and complete a controlled handover to the METRO team by the planned September 2026 go-live and October 2026 hypercare transition.

3.2.content:
- Implement SAP Cloud ALM tenant setup and onboarding for METRO’s agreed landscape.
- Configure SAP Cloud ALM Standard Change Management and ChaRM-related transport governance.
- Enable Technical Monitoring for non-production systems, including alerts, notifications, and dashboards.
- Validate Dev and QA change cycles end-to-end before production integration.
- Integrate production systems into ChaRM and operational monitoring use cases by go-live.
- Train METRO users and support transition of operations during hypercare.
- Align Cloud ALM delivery milestones with the S/4 RISE migration timeline.

3.3.content:
The target state is a governed SAP Cloud ALM operating model in which METRO uses one platform for technical monitoring and change execution aligned to the S/4 migration schedule. The engagement begins with subscription, onboarding, landscape identification, and readiness configuration. It then progresses into definition of monitoring use cases, transport governance, and role-based access, followed by configuration of Technical Monitoring and Change Request Management, end-to-end testing in Dev and QA, and production integration for both change and operations use cases. The final state includes active dashboards, alerting, documented operating procedures, trained METRO users, and transition to METRO-owned support.

The indicative process flow is: onboard SAP Cloud ALM → confirm landscape, roles, and monitoring use cases → configure data flow, transport routes, and release strategies → enable monitoring, alerts, and dashboards for non-production systems → execute Dev and QA ChaRM test cycles → map production into ChaRM and operations use cases → deploy to production in September 2026 → complete hypercare, knowledge transfer, and transition in October 2026.

4.1.content: The services under this SOW cover METRO locations and Bristlecone offshore delivery center(s). Scope includes remote delivery, configuration, testing, training, and hypercare support for the agreed SAP Cloud ALM landscape supporting METRO’s S/4 RISE migration plan. Any country-specific rollout, local compliance, or language localization beyond the agreed METRO landscape is excluded unless added through change control.

4.2.content: In-scope business processes are limited to SAP Cloud ALM processes required for Technical Monitoring and Change Request Management. This includes standard change workflow definition, transport governance across Dev, QA, and Production, monitoring use-case definition, alert and notification handling, issue resolution support during hypercare, and transition of agreed operating procedures to the METRO team. Monitoring scope covers system health, application monitoring, job monitoring, user performance monitoring, and integration monitoring for the agreed landscape.

4.3.content:
Technical scope includes SAP Cloud ALM tenant onboarding and subaccount setup, landscape identification, prerequisite readiness configuration, SAP landscape and data flow configuration to SAP Cloud ALM, user and role setup, transport route and release strategy configuration, and configuration of Technical Monitoring and ChaRM-related workflows. The engagement includes Dev and QA end-to-end ChaRM test cycles, production system mapping in ChaRM, monitoring enablement for non-production systems, production integration in ChaRM and operations use cases, dashboards, alerts, and notifications. Integration technologies in scope include the agreed SAP integration landscape supporting S/4HANA Cloud, BTP applications, MII, and Integration Suite/CPI-based data flows.

Functional coverage includes SAP landscape management, system health monitoring, application monitoring, job monitoring, user performance monitoring in S/4HANA, integration monitoring, and notification and alert management. 5.content:
The solution architecture is based on SAP Cloud ALM as the central SaaS platform for Technical Monitoring and Change Request Management for the agreed METRO landscape. SAP Cloud ALM will be used to onboard the tenant and subaccount, manage landscape and data-flow connectivity, configure standard change workflows, and enable monitoring, dashboards, alerts, and notifications across the in-scope SAP environment.

The deployment model is a phased implementation aligned to the S/4 RISE migration timeline. Initial activities cover subscription, onboarding, landscape identification, and prerequisite configuration, followed by transport governance design, monitoring use-case finalization, and user/role setup. Configuration and validation then proceed across Dev and QA for ChaRM and non-production monitoring, with production system mapping, production integration, and hypercare completed by September–October 2026.

<IMAGE id="a9602c43b0d1"/>

Architecture scope includes SAP S/4HANA Cloud, SAP BTP applications, SAP MII, and Integration Suite/CPI-based flows connected to SAP Cloud ALM for system health, application, job, user performance, and integration monitoring, together with ChaRM workflow enablement for governed transport movement from Dev to QA to Production.

Change governance will use SAP Cloud ALM standard change management with defined transport routes, release strategies, configurable approvals, and end-to-end testing before production deployment. Bristlecone’s Cloud ALM Architect will design and implement the solution in coordination with the METRO governance team, METRO single point of contact for ChaRM inputs, and the METRO core testing team. <TECH TEAM: confirm whether any additional non-SAP systems or monitoring endpoints are to be connected in this phase>

6.1.content:
The engagement will be delivered in a phased implementation model aligned to METRO’s S/4 RISE migration timeline. Work starts with SAP Cloud ALM subscription readiness, technical onboarding, landscape identification, and connectivity planning. The design phase will confirm monitoring use cases, metric values, user and role alignment, and the target transport governance model.

Build and validation activities will then run across two delivery tracks: Change Request Management and Technical Monitoring. ChaRM scope includes workflow configuration, transport routes, release strategies, and end-to-end Dev and QA test cycles. Technical Monitoring scope includes landscape data flow setup, health monitoring, job and automation monitoring, user performance monitoring, integration and exception monitoring, and alert and notification configuration. Deployment will complete production system mapping in ChaRM, enable agreed production operations use cases, and transition support to METRO through training, SOP updates, hypercare, and knowledge transfer.

16.1.content:
Milestone tracking for this engagement will be governed by the project phases in Section 6.2, the deliverables in Section 9, and the commercials in Section 13. Payment and invoice events, where milestone-based, shall align to completion and acceptance of the applicable deliverables rather than elapsed time alone.

The milestone deliverables matrix shall map, at minimum, the following control points: SAP Cloud ALM subscription initiation; onboarding and connectivity planning completion; finalized monitoring use cases and metric values; prerequisite readiness and data-flow configuration; configured change workflow and transport governance; completed Dev and QA end-to-end ChaRM test cycle; non-production monitoring, dashboard, alert, and notification setup; production integration in ChaRM and operations use cases; and hypercare transition, knowledge transfer, and documentation handover.

Any variance between planned milestone completion, accepted deliverables, and commercial trigger points shall be handled through the change control process in Section 17.

16.2.content:
- Final confirmation of the detailed monitoring metric thresholds and alert values shall be completed before configuration finalization.
- Final user and role matrix for SAP Cloud ALM shall be completed before authorization testing and production readiness.
- Final escalation matrix, RCA process, and monitoring schedule shall be agreed before deploy and hypercare.
- Any request to include capabilities listed in the exclusions section shall be treated as new scope and managed through change control.
- Any expansion beyond the agreed METRO landscape, monitoring use cases, or change workflows shall be frozen only after approved scope, timeline, and commercial impact are documented.

16.3.content:
- Integration scope is limited to the interfaces and landscape connections identified in Section 4.6 for SAP S/4HANA Cloud, SAP BTP applications, SAP MII, Integration Suite/CPI, and agreed production operations use cases.
- Any additional interface, endpoint, landscape, or monitoring target requested after scope baseline approval shall require impact assessment and approved change control before work starts.
- Production integration shall proceed only after Dev and QA ChaRM cycle validation and prerequisite readiness are completed.
- Scope excludes custom development outside standard SAP Cloud ALM configuration.
- If METRO requires non-standard extensions, bespoke monitoring logic, or custom workflow behavior, Bristlecone will assess feasibility, effort, timeline, and commercials before any commitment is made.
- Configuration changes affecting transport routes, release strategies, or production system mapping shall be reviewed jointly by Bristlecone and METRO governance leads before implementation.

16.4.content:
All changes to scope, deliverables, timeline, delivery approach, staffing assumptions, or commercials shall be managed through the Change Management Process set out in Section 17. No work outside the approved scope shall be performed on an informal instruction alone.

A change request shall be raised where there is any expansion of landscape coverage, monitoring use cases, integration points, production operations scope, role design effort, testing cycles, or hypercare obligations. Each change request shall document the requested change, delivery impact, dependency impact, and commercial impact before approval.

Approved changes shall be reflected in the applicable SOW baseline, project plan, deliverables, and commercials. Rejected or deferred changes shall not be treated as included scope.

17.content:
Changes to scope, timeline, deliverables, assumptions, or commercials will be managed through a formal Change Request process. No work outside the approved scope will proceed until the related Change Request is assessed and approved by both parties.

| Step | Activity | Owner | Timeline |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CR raised | METRO or Bristlecone project team identifies a requested change to scope, deliverables, milestone dates, landscape coverage, monitoring use cases, transport governance, production integration, or transition activities and submits the request to the project governance team. | Within 1 business day of identifying the change |
| 2 | CR logged | Bristlecone Project Management records the Change Request in the project change log, assigns a tracking ID, and captures the request description, reason, originator, and date raised. | Within 1 business day of receipt |
| 3 | Impact assessment | Bristlecone Project Management and Cloud ALM Architect assess impact on scope, effort, schedule, dependencies, testing, go-live readiness, and commercials, with input from METRO stakeholders as needed. | Within 3 business days of logging |
| 4 | CR reviewed / approved | METRO Project Governance Team and Bristlecone Project Management review the impact assessment and approve, reject, or defer the Change Request. | Within 5 business days of impact assessment completion |
| 5 | SOW amendment / addendum | For approved changes affecting contractual scope, dates, deliverables, or commercials, the parties document the approved change through an amendment, addendum, or other agreed written change instrument before execution of the changed work. | Before affected work starts |
| 6 | CR closure | Bristlecone Project Management updates the change log with final status, implementation date, and reference to the approval record, and communicates closure to the project team. | Within 1 business day of approval implementation or rejection |

Change control applies to any expansion beyond the agreed METRO landscape, monitoring use cases, change workflows, production integration activities, or hypercare and transition scope. Changes required due to deviation from agreed assumptions, including landscape readiness, role mapping, monitoring use-case finalization, cutover readiness, or METRO transition alignment, will follow the same process.

19.2.content: Either party may terminate this SOW for cause upon written notice if the other party materially breaches this SOW and fails to cure that breach within the applicable cure period under the governing agreement. Either party may also terminate immediately if the other party becomes insolvent, enters liquidation or bankruptcy proceedings, ceases to conduct business in the ordinary course, or engages in fraud, wilful misconduct, or unlawful activity materially affecting this SOW. If termination for cause results from METRO’s breach, Bristlecone will be entitled to payment for services performed and non-cancellable commitments incurred up to the termination date.

19.3.content: On termination or expiry of this SOW, Bristlecone will cease the terminated services, deliver all completed work products due for handover under this SOW, and reasonably support transition of configured SAP Cloud ALM Technical Monitoring and Change Request Management activities to METRO for the agreed handover period through October 2026, if termination occurs near planned project close. Each party will return or securely destroy the other party’s confidential information in accordance with the governing agreement, except where retention is required by law or internal recordkeeping policy. Termination will not affect accrued payment obligations, rights that arose before termination, or provisions that survive by their nature, including confidentiality, intellectual property, liability, audit, and dispute-resolution terms to the extent stated in the governing agreement.
